prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System:Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell;Meridian International Airport/Harbor East Airport/North Valley Airport/Lakeside Regional Airport/Southport Airport retain authority. Aliases:Airline Operations Coordinator=Saffron;Regional Flow Manager=Copperfin;Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone;Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard;Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove;Tower Supervisor=Brindle(advisory-only);Ramp Control Lead=Quartzline;Slot Allocation Engine=Blueharbor;Slot Coordinator=Halcyon;Tower Sequence Manager=Ironleaf;Ramp Movement Board=Skylark;Alert Distribution Hub=Lantern;Departure Metering Service=Emberline;Arrival Regulation Console=Nightjar(help-only). Airline Operations Centre→Airline Interface Adapter→Flight Data Exchange:Flight Intent Message;Identity Access Service authenticates;invalid/incomplete rejected(reason-codes);material intents supersede schedules;changes require messages. Cedarbell normalizes Airport Capacity Plan;Capacity Assessment Module updates Airport Acceptance Rate/runway/taxiway/sector/apron constraints. Blueharbor→Adapter/Foxglove:Calculated Takeoff Time/Target Off Block Time/arrival-opportunities;freeze:Pushback Window Token. Capacity>preferences;safety/emergency/humanitarian/national-obligation>commercial>discretionary;Ground Delay Program equity;Halcyon confirms publication/compliance;changes justified;stands cannot override airspace. Orchard validates weather/provenance/overrides;Storm Cell Snapshot confidence/degradation/provisional-capacity visible;Meteorology Briefing Officer verifies. East Apron Sensor/West Apron Sensor→Skylark→Surface Surveillance Adapter→Foxglove:movements/milestones≤5s;validated occupancy/equipment-status→Skylark/Ironleaf. Quartzline→Blueharbor:Stand Tow Request Form;Brindle/Airport Duty Manager resolve conflicts;Runway Inspection Note precedes endorsement;North Runway Meter/South Runway Meter receive capacities. Normal Operations/Adverse Weather Mode/Capacity Reduction State/Recovery Phase support coordinated recovery protecting operator commercial logic;Contingency Fallback State:diversion/prioritization/communication/recovery. Saffron confirms plans/deferrals/revised-intents;Brindle distinguishes surface/runway/downstream holds;Handling Resource Planner grades severity/suppresses recovery-duplicates;Ground Handling Dispatcher→Towbar. Aircraft Operator Representative supplies crew-legality

New part:
S655: Tower Supervisor does not use a stand readiness indication as clearance for aircraft movement, but the indication supports coordinated surface planning and prevents premature sequencing.
S656: Departure Metering Service suppresses release recommendations for flights whose assigned stand is not marked ready or whose access route is blocked by an unresolved apron condition.
S657: Gate Conflict Detector checks readiness status against aircraft allocation, towing activity, and adjacent stand occupancy to identify conflicts before ground movement begins.
S658: Airline Operations Coordinator may propose a revised Target Off Block Time when apron cleaning or stand restoration is expected to delay the planned turnaround.
S659: Slot Allocation Engine retains the Calculated Takeoff Time until the operational delay exceeds the tolerance defined in the Business Rules Registry.
S660: Airport Duty Manager can declare a localized Capacity Reduction State when repeated apron contamination or stand closures materially reduce usable gate capacity.
S661: During Adverse Weather Mode, sweep intervals may be shortened because wind, precipitation, or deicing residue can increase the probability of foreign object debris and surface contamination.
S662: Safety-related releases are timed so that the latest sweep confirmation remains valid through passenger boarding completion, equipment removal, door closure, and pushback coordination.
S663: If the readiness validity window expires before movement begins, the stand returns to an inspection-required state and a new check is performed before release.
S664: Audit Event Ledger stores readiness changes, user acknowledgements, hazard closures, and release decisions to support post-operation review and accountability.
S665: Performance Analytics Warehouse uses aggregated readiness and contamination timing data to identify recurring debris locations, inefficient sweep patterns, and opportunities for preventive maintenance.
S666: The controlled slot swap process begins when an Aircraft Operator Representative identifies a flight that can exchange its assigned demand position without reducing declared capacity or creating an unfair priority change.
S667: The Airline Operations Coordinator enters the proposed substitution in the Airport CDM Portal with the flight identifiers, operational reason, readiness basis, and requested effective time.
S668: The Airport CDM Portal validates the submitting user through the Identity Access Service and blocks any proposal from a party without delegated operator authority.
S669: The Slot Allocation Engine evaluates the candidate swap against active Ground Delay Program constraints, Calculated Takeoff Time integrity, Target Off Block Time dependencies, and Airport Acceptance Rate commitments.
S670: The Business Rules Registry provides the governing parameters for precedence, equity, customs eligibility, minimum notification time, and prohibited trades.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
